sources.title: Michael W. Davis, The Geometry and Topology of Coxeter Groups (first-edition author manuscript, 2007-2008)
sources.locator: Chapter 6, Section 6.9 (Theorem 6.9.1 and Table 6.1 of irreducible spherical and Euclidean diagrams, printed pp. 103-104) and Section 6.12 (Theorem 6.12.9 with its proof, printed pp. 119-120); Appendix C in full (printed pp. 433-438): Theorem C.1.2, Theorem C.1.3, Theorem C.1.4, Lemma C.2.1, Lemma C.2.2, Lemma C.2.3, Table C.1, Lemma C.3.1 and the proofs of Theorems C.1.2-C.1.4; Theorem D.1.1 and Corollary D.1.3 (printed p. 440) for the disjointness of open chambers and discreteness of the canonical image.

contents.name: Theorem 6.12.9 (i) equivalent to (ii): W is a reflection group on S^{n-1} (a spherical simplex exists) exactly when the cosine matrix is positive definite, via Theorem 6.4.3 and Proposition 6.8.2
contents.reason: This pair uses the selected arithmetic route to the criterion: positive definiteness is decided by the exclusions and determinant lemma, and the implication from positive definiteness to finiteness is proved by dual-chamber isolation plus compactness of the orthogonal group. The spherical-simplex developing-map equivalence (i) is deliberately not built, matching the run's design choice.

contents.name: Theorem 6.12.9 (iii) implies (ii): for finite W the canonical representation is semisimple and irreducible, and every invariant inner product is proportional to B (Lemma 6.6.1, Corollary 6.12.8, Lemma 6.12.2)
Theorem D.1.1 (Tits) and Corollary D.1.3: open chambers have pairwise disjoint interiors, and the canonical and dual images are discrete subgroups of GL(E)
Theorem C.1.2 (classification of finite Coxeter groups) with the left-hand column of Table 6.1
Theorem C.1.3 and the right-hand column of Table 6.1 (classification of Euclidean Coxeter groups: positive semidefinite of corank one)
contents.reason: Positive semidefinite diagrams of corank one and their classification are exactly the subject of the later affine classification page of this run; this pair records the semidefinite witnesses as exclusions only and does not claim the Euclidean list.

contents.name: Theorem C.1.4 and Table 6.2 (classification of hyperbolic simplicial Coxeter groups of type (n,1) with all proper subdiagrams positive definite)
contents.reason: No item of this pair makes a statement about Lorentzian signature, hyperbolic simplices or the (n,1) case, so the hyperbolic classification is not built; the exclusions here stop at the positive definite list.

contents.name: Lemma C.2.1 with Table C.1: the left-column diagrams are positive definite, with det(2A) equal to n+1 (A_n), 2 (B_n), 4 (D_n), 3/2/1 (E_6,E_7,E_8), 1 (F_4), 3-sqrt5 (H_3), (7-3sqrt5)/2 (H_4)
Table C.1 rows for the non-crystallographic types H_3 and H_4 (det(2A) = 3-sqrt5 and (7-3sqrt5)/2) and the rank-two determinant det A = sin^2(pi/m) for I_2(m)
Table C.1 row det(2A)(B_n) = 2 and the identity of the B_n and C_n diagrams in Table 6.1
Formulas (C.1) and (C.2): det 2A = 2 d_{n-1} - d_{n-2} for a final edge of label 3 and det 2A = 2 d_{n-1} - 2 d_{n-2} for a final edge of label 4
Lemma C.2.2 and its proof: the right-column diagrams (cycles and the other affine diagrams) are positive semidefinite of corank one, the cycle witness being the all-ones vector (rows summing to zero)
Lemma C.2.3: the star-shaped diagrams Z_4 and Z_5 (label-5 extensions) have negative determinant
Lemma C.3.1 and its proof (domination): if an irreducible positive semidefinite diagram strictly dominates another, the dominated diagram is positive definite

Proofs of Theorems C.1.2-C.1.3 (printed pp. 437-438): the exclusion chain - rank at least 3, no infinite label, tree, unique branch vertex of valence 3, arm inequalities a=1, b<=2, c<=4, then m>=4, at most one label > 3, no branch vertices, F_4, then H_3/H_4
Theorem 6.9.1 (Lanner) and the spherical/Euclidean/hyperbolic trichotomy of simplicial Coxeter groups
contents.reason: The trichotomy of the geometric representation is not needed by this pair, which classifies abstract Coxeter systems by positivity of the cosine form; no Tits-cone interior or hyperbolic geometry statement is made here.

contents.name: Corollary 6.12.11 (faithfulness of the canonical representation) and Corollary 6.12.12 (virtual torsion-freeness via Selberg)
contents.reason: Faithfulness is supplied independently by the earlier page canonical-roots-signs-and-faithful-reflections of this run; virtual torsion-freeness needs Selberg's lemma and belongs to the general Coxeter-group theory, not to the finite classification.

sources.title: Jean Michel, Lectures on Coxeter groups (Beijing lecture notes, April-May 2014)
sources.locator: Section 5 'Classification of finite Coxeter groups': the preliminary list of finite irreducible types and the table of cosines (printed pp. 12-13), Proposition 5.14 with proof (printed pp. 12-13), Theorem 5.15 with its two-part proof, printed pp. 13-15; Exercise 5.16 on integrality (printed p. 15) only as an out-of-scope remark.

contents.name: Preliminary list and conventions before Theorem 5.15: A_n, B_n/C_n, D_n, E_n, F_4, H_n, I_2(e) and the identification of the Weyl types, with I_2(2)=A_1 x A_1, I_2(3)=A_2, I_2(4)=B_2 and G_2=I_2(6)
Proposition 5.14(i): V is irreducible exactly when the Coxeter graph is connected

Proposition 5.14(ii) with proof: W is finite exactly when B(Gamma) is positive definite; the 'only if' direction averages an invariant form, the 'if' direction uses compactness of the orthogonal group and discreteness of the canonical image through the neighbourhood {g in GL(V*) : g(x) in C}
Lemma 5.7: a W-invariant bilinear form on an irreducible representation is unique up to scalar (used in Proposition 5.14(ii))

Theorem 5.15, first part: determinants det C(An)=n+1, det C(Bn)=2, det C(Dn)=4, det C(E6)=3, det C(E7)=2, det C(E8)=1, det C(F4)=1, det C(I2(m))=4(1-cos^2(pi/m)), det C(H3)=3-sqrt5, det C(H4)=(7-3sqrt5)/2, proving the listed diagrams positive definite

Theorem 5.15, second part, properties (i)-(vii) of a connected spherical graph: subgraphs are spherical; no circuit (witness v = sum of the e_{s_i}); sum over neighbours <e_s,e_j>^2 < 1 with the resulting valency and label restrictions; the gluing/folding step; at most one edge of label > 3 and at most one degree-3 vertex, with a chain when a large label occurs; the chain inequality (i+1)(j+1) > 4ij cos^2(pi/m) and its cases; the three-chain inequality 1/(p+1)+1/(q+1)+1/(r+1) > 1
The chain case enumeration of Theorem 5.15 (possibilities (1,j) and (2,2) for a label of order > 3, and the boundary triples (1,2,5), (2,2,2), (1,3,3) of the three-chain inequality)
Exercise 5.16: an integral representation forces m in {2,3,4,6,infinity}, with the converse for crystallographic Cartan matrices
contents.reason: Integrality and crystallographic realizations belong to the later crystallographic and affine pages of this run; this pair classifies arbitrary Coxeter matrices, including the non-crystallographic H and I_2(m) types, and makes no integrality claim.
